findings.claim: MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep changes the depth check from `>=` to `>`, so one extra nesting level is accepted: with MaximumObjectGraphDepth = N, an object graph of depth N+1 is no longer rejected. This loosens the recursion/depth limit that protects against stack exhaustion on untrusted data. It is also unrelated to the SuppressSourceGeneration analyzer fix. The ledger (L18) records no decision for it beyond 'follow the requirement', and the requirement does not mention it. Existing depth-limit tests that assume a graph at exactly the maximum depth throws would likely fail.

receipt_plan.detail: Build a nested array/map payload whose depth equals MaximumObjectGraphDepth (e.g. MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(N)) and deserialize it with base-built and head-built code. Base throws InsufficientExecutionStackException; head succeeds. Also rerun the existing MessagePackSecurityTests depth tests.
